I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the core system on my farm, it matches local conditions in southern Hebei, and I have well irrigation so I can support a relatively stable, input-responsive grain system. I will still keep a smaller cotton area because it spreads risk and gives me some cash-crop income, but I will not let cotton take too much land away from the grain rotation. Since I am educated and already have four years of farming experience, I will run a fairly disciplined plan: improved or hybrid seed, moderate-to-high fertilizer rates, timely irrigation from the well, and enough pesticide use to protect yield without spraying excessively. For wheat, I will push for a solid, stable yield with three irrigations and balanced nitrogen-led fertilization. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed and no-tillage seeding to save time and preserve moisture during the tight turnaround. For cotton, I will use improved seed, plough the field before establishment, irrigate more times than grain, and manage insects more actively because cotton is more management-intensive. My aim is steady output, good labor organization for a four-person household, and lower production risk rather than chasing the absolute maximum yield.
